findings.decompiled: mem[0] = 0xf5b90f0c...3f19 / mem[0] = 0 / mem[0] = 0x82db5943...30f5 / mem[0] = 0 / mem[0] = 0x82db5943...30f5 / mem[32] = 0 / mem[0] = caller / mem[32] = sha3(0x82db..., 0) / if not hasRole[0x82db...][caller]:
findings.issue: Each role check carries 8 scratch-memory stores; the hashes they feed are already printed as hasRole[role][caller], and four of them are overwritten by the very next store to mem[0] with no read in between, so they are dead even without alias analysis (P8, about 300 lines).
findings.rule: A store to mem[a] (width w) is dead when the next access to [a, a + w) on every path is a store covering it, with no read of that range, call, sha3, log, return or revert in between; and stores whose only reader is a sha3 already printed with its arguments are dead.

notes: Source loops (7, all whiles with readable bounds): the for loops of applyInlineConnectionConfigUpdates (2260), applySubsetTokenUpdates, getCurrentRateLimiterStateBatch, getFeeBatch (2570, with 'delete fees[i]' shown as a fresh zeroed struct, as solc does), getLaneVerificationBatch, getTokenConfigBatch, getTokenTransferFeeConfigBatch. The pack's reach lists include ConnectionPolicyStore/FeePolicyStore/SecurityPolicyStore and FinalityCodec code that runs in the external stores, not in this bytecode; their loops are not counted. The other 79 whiles are implicit ABI loops: calldata arrays re-encoded for the forwarded calls (with per-element checks), decoding of returned struct arrays, and encoding of returned struct arrays (nested ones as 'while True' with the return inside); bytes members are copy lines (MCOPY on cancun). P7 counts the memory-to-memory array encodings/decodings. Role checks, AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount reverts, Address.functionCall's AddressEmptyCode / FailedCall handling match the source.
summary: Faithful; the seven source loops are clear whiles, but every role check drags dead scratch-memory stores and decoded structs show as memory slices.
